description: Sync the events on every calendar of one Google account, one searchable event card per event.
opening: Sync events from every calendar on one Google account's calendar list. Each event is one document that reads as a short event card: title, time, place, organizer, attendees and description. A changed occurrence of a recurring meeting links to its series.

Google Calendar sharing and event visibility are not imported, so private events are visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. You cannot pick individual calendars: every calendar on the account's list is synced. The first sync picks events by when they were last edited, not by when they take place. An event cancelled after it was synced can stay in HydraDB.

notes: Private events are synced like any other event.

connect.auth: Google Calendar uses a Google OAuth 2.0 client id and client secret, with a refresh token for the Google account to sync.

credentials.name: refresh_token
credentials.text: A refresh token for the Google account, issued with a Calendar read scope such as `calendar.readonly`.

steps.title: Get a client and refresh token
steps.text: Get a Google OAuth 2.0 client id and secret, and a refresh token for the account whose calendars you want to sync. Issue the token with a Calendar read scope such as `calendar.readonly`.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the three values as `client_id`, `client_secret` and `refresh_token`.

steps.title: Select the account
steps.text: HydraDB lists one item, All data, that covers every calendar on the account's list. Select it.

connect.account: One connector reads one Google account. Every calendar on that account's calendar list is synced.

sync.first_sync: Reads events last edited within the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default. When an event has no edit time, its creation time is used. Events with neither are read regardless. The window is about edits, not meeting dates: an old recurring meeting that was not edited recently may not be picked up, and a future event edited recently is.
sync.changes: Each sync reads, calendar by calendar, the events edited since the last sync.
sync.edits: An edited event is read again and replaces its document.
sync.deletes: Cancelled events are not added. An event cancelled after it was synced can stay searchable in HydraDB.

documents.name: Events
documents.one_document: One calendar event. A recurring series is one document for the series, plus one for each occurrence that was changed. An event that appears with the same event id on more than one calendar of the account is one document, and each calendar's copy can replace the other.
documents.title: The event title, or `Calendar event <id>` when it has none.
documents.text: The title, then a `When` line with the start and end, a `Where` line with the location, an `Organizer` line, an `Attendees` line, then the event description. Descriptions are kept as Google supplies them, so an HTML description keeps its markup. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the event was last edited, else when it was created. It is not the time the event takes place.
documents.files: None. Event attachments are not synced.

attributes.name: organizer
attributes.text: The organizer's display name, or email when there is no name, written as the `Organizer` line. The same name is kept as `author`. The organizer is not attached to the event as a person in the graph unless the same email is also among the attendees.

attributes.name: attendees
attributes.text: Each attendee's email, display name and response status. Names, or emails when there is no name, are written as the `Attendees` line. The graph attaches each attendee to the event by email. Response statuses are kept on the event but are not searchable.

attributes.name: location
attributes.text: The free-text location, written as the `Where` line.

attributes.name: start_at
attributes.text: The scheduled start, or the date for an all-day event, written in the `When` line. It does not set the result date.

attributes.name: end_at
attributes.text: The scheduled end, or the date for an all-day event, written after the start in the `When` line when the event has a start.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the event was last edited. Sets the result date and decides which events each sync reads. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the event was created. Sets the result date only when the event has no edit time. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Recurring series
attributes.text: For a changed occurrence, the recurring series event it belongs to. Links the occurrence to the series document. Not searchable.

attributes.name: thread_id
attributes.text: The recurring series an occurrence belongs to, empty for one-off events. Groups the occurrences of one series together in the graph. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
attributes.text: The calendar's id. Limits a query to one calendar. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
attributes.text: The calendar's name. Limits a query to a calendar by name. Not searchable: the calendar name is not part of the event text.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's events. Not searchable.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: `confirmed` or `tentative`. It is not part of the event text.

example_searches: What was the agenda in the description of last Tuesday's planning meeting?
Which meetings did Dana organize this month?
Where is the offsite being held?

connections: A changed occurrence of a recurring meeting to its series.
Changed occurrences of the same series to each other, so they group together.
No links to other tools, including Gmail invitations.
people: The organizer only when the organizer is also an attendee.
Attendee names and response statuses are kept with the event but do not identify people in the graph.
graph.from_text: The event card: title, time, place, organizer, attendees and description.

not_synced: Calendar sharing and event visibility settings.
Event attachments, audio and video, and conference details beyond what the location or description says.
Unchanged occurrences of a recurring series as documents of their own.
Events last edited before the first sync's window.
Cancellations: an event cancelled after it was synced can stay in HydraDB.
